nutshell: Today's items point to agents and coding tools moving into everyday workflows, from MCP-connected services to multi-agent coding and self-improving agent harnesses. Model news centers on frequent Qwen and GGUF releases and on OpenAI adjusting usage limits as its products merge, while most research output is incremental work on robotics, video and world models. items.title: Tell HN: Lots of Ask HNs again
items.snippet: There have been questions about why the /ask page ( https://news.ycombinator.com/ask ) was running dry of Ask HNs - e.g.: Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984484 - Oct 2026 (47 comments) Ask HN: Why is pagination gone on "Ask HN", and showing only 19 items? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50280719 - Oct 2026 (3 comments) I believe I found the problem. The pool of stories for https://news.ycombinator.com/ask has traditionally been drawn from the ranked stories list from which we generate the frontpage. That list is restricted to the top 1500 ranked submissions, and it seems the % of submissions which are text posts (i.e. no linked URL) had declined enough to starve the Ask HN feed. The solution is to compute a separate list of ranked Ask HNs. p.s. "Ask HN" is the conventional name but it means text posts. The title can also start with "Tell HN" or nothing in particular. They're just posts which were submitted without a URL.

items.title: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock
items.snippet: Proactive assistants that guide people through physical tasks must decide, every few seconds, whether a step is complete and whether a mistake has occurred. We find that two benchmarks for this task largely reward knowing when rather than seeing what: a timer that never looks at the video, raising an alarm at 25 s and confirming each step at 30 s, reaches a mistake F1 of 0.373 on Ego-MC-Bench, above every published result (at most 0.27). We formalize this as the video-blind frontier, the best t…
items.summary: A paper argues proactive task assistants should wait for visual evidence rather than a timer when judging step completion.

items.title: Puzzling-Bench: Evaluating Language Models on 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles with Community-Verified Answers
items.snippet: We introduce Puzzling-Bench, a benchmark of 23,777 puzzles with community-verified answers drawn from the Puzzling Stack Exchange archive (2014-2026): riddles, ciphers, logic grids, lateral-thinking problems, wordplay and recreational mathematics, a third of them with images. Every puzzle carries the answer accepted by its author, a short reference answer taken from it (LLM-extracted for the evaluation sets and checked on a 50-puzzle human review), the author's own hints, community tags and a c…
items.summary: Puzzling-Bench is a benchmark of 23,777 community-verified puzzles for evaluating language models.

items.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
items.snippet: Lembas treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget, using an iterative water-filling algorithm and attention reuse to improve long-video and multi-turn understanding with fewer tokens and less compute.
items.summary: Lembas treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles to cut tokens and compute.

items.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.snippet: ELITE enables coding agents to self-improve by integrating complementary implementation mechanisms from independently generated improvements without using downstream task evaluations in the evolution loop, achieving strong SWE-bench performance and transfer.
items.summary: ELITE lets coding agents self-improve by combining implementation mechanisms without downstream evaluations in the loop, with strong SWE-bench results.

items.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
items.snippet: SPLICE improves reinforcement learning on long-horizon agent tasks by constructing local training targets from failed trajectories using a proposal model to select splice points and generate bounded options, outperforming GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines.
items.summary: SPLICE builds local training targets from failed agent trajectories to improve long-horizon agent reinforcement learning.

items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.snippet: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. In trajectory collection, teacher…
items.summary: Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative to fully online on-policy distillation for long-horizon agents.

items.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
items.snippet: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonst…
items.summary: DemoFoundry uses coding agents and generative rendering to produce photorealistic robot demonstration data.

items.title: Change the Base, Change the Game: Rethinking Pan-sharpening
items.snippet: Many pan-sharpening (PS) networks reconstruct high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) images by adding learned residuals to 4times-interpolated low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) inputs, incorporating panchromatic (PAN) detail only through these residual corrections. This raises a simple question: Why start with a blurry base when sharp spatial detail is already available? We propose PanBase, a sharper multispectral starting point designed for more effective residual learning. Guided by physical…
items.summary: The paper argues that pan-sharpening networks should change their base representation rather than add residuals to interpolated inputs.

items.title: LiveVAE: Causal Window Attention Makes Efficient Streaming Video VAE
items.snippet: While video diffusion models have grown faster and increasingly streamable, the video VAE remains a primary latency bottleneck across interactive generation and editing pipelines. Existing VAEs and their acceleration methods rely mainly on heavy convolutions or full frame attention, and most focus only on decoding, leaving encoding costly for streaming conditional generation and editing. This raises a natural question: Do video VAE encoding and decoding actually require such global spatiotempor…
items.summary: LiveVAE uses causal window attention to make a streaming video VAE faster for interactive generation.

items.title: OmniPersist: Persistent Dynamic World Modeling via Coupled Panoramic Evolution
items.snippet: Action-conditioned world models play a vital role in robotics and autonomous driving, yet existing video diffusion models struggle to maintain dynamic object persistence. When the camera turns away and returns, out-of-view moving entities fail to evolve plausibly in latent space, often mutating or vanishing entirely due to bounded perspective views. To resolve this issue, we propose OmniPersist, a unified framework that couples perspective video generation with panoramic evolution within a sing…
items.summary: OmniPersist couples panoramic evolution to keep out-of-view dynamic objects persistent in action-conditioned world models.

items.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
items.snippet: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically relies on a verifier that can reliably judge whether sampled solutions are correct. However, in many realistic settings, complete verification is generally unavailable, while cheap checks can only falsify failures. We formalize this regime as one-sided verifiability (OSV): verified negatives are reliable counterexamples, but verified positives are merely non-falsified candidates and may contain many false positives. This asymmetry…
items.summary: Negative-only policy optimization extends reinforcement learning to settings where only failures can be cheaply verified.

items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.snippet: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies t…
items.summary: AIChipBench benchmarks LLM coding agents on automated AI accelerator hardware design, including stateful decoder bugs.

items.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
items.snippet: WorldBridge generates coherent and controllable 3D worlds from scattered, low-overlap images by encoding references into a global scene context and using attention and latent-reference consistency optimization.
items.summary: WorldBridge generates coherent 3D worlds from scattered low-overlap images using a global scene context.

items.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift
items.snippet: Reasoning-based candidate selection in small language models for entity disambiguation yields negligible in-domain gains but becomes decisive under true zero-shot domain shift, with reranker uncertainty and shift explaining when the paradigms disagree.
items.summary: A study finds reasoning-based candidate selection in small LLMs gives little in-domain gain but helps under zero-shot domain shift.

items.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
items.snippet: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls…
items.summary: An evaluation of 25 open-weight decision models across 17 tasks in many languages finds calibration gaps outside English.

items.title: A Mesh for Every Moment
items.snippet: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame. Existing dynamic Gaussian splatting methods either model appearance alone or target isolated objects segmented by foreground masks, and all of them recover meshes by TSDF fusion or Poisson reconstruction, whose fixed grids limit the detail they can capture. At the core of MEMO is a per-Gaussian motion model…
items.summary: MEMO reconstructs complete dynamic scenes from multiple synchronized cameras and extracts a mesh at every frame.

items.title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
items.snippet: SPARC uses geometry-guided pruning of self-attention in pretrained video diffusion transformers to unify camera control and persistent scene memory, improving camera adherence and revisit consistency while greatly reducing computation.
items.summary: SPARC prunes self-attention in video diffusion transformers to unify camera control and scene memory for long videos.

items.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
items.snippet: GOLD-SLAM integrates panoramic Gaussian splatting with LiDAR depth priors for omnidirectional SLAM, improving pose estimation and geometric reconstruction while maintaining competitive rendering quality.
items.summary: GOLD-SLAM integrates panoramic Gaussian splatting with LiDAR depth for omnidirectional SLAM.

items.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
items.snippet: SimPWM uses a parameter-free simulator as a proxy to generate robot videos and simulated states, revealing that video models follow arm motion more reliably than object dynamics and often ignore simulated object state.
items.summary: SimPWM uses a simulator as a proxy to generate robot videos and finds video models follow arm motion more reliably than object dynamics.

items.title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
items.snippet: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. We introduce SOLVE, a training-free, versatile and efficient agent policy: a multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. The agent decides the number and spacing of keyposes for both fast long-range…
items.summary: SOLVE uses a multimodal LLM agent to write sparse, ordered 6-DoF keyposes for robot manipulation, reducing inference cost.
